algorithm.count: the compare uses the element count (end - begin) >> 4, not the byte length
algorithm.flag_set: a nonzero flag byte at holder + 0x10 reverses the range in place (16-byte element swaps front-to-back until the cursors cross) and the flag byte is cleared to zero before the sum runs; empty and single-element ranges reverse to themselves but the flag is still cleared
algorithm.null_pair: a null range pointer substitutes the global pair at 0x6500780 (begin) and 0x6500788 (end) and ignores the flag byte entirely; those slots sit in a BSS tail, so they start as zero, which is the empty-range false answer
algorithm.reverse_dead_block: the post-sum reversal block (loop at 0x5d533b8, flag cleared at 0x5d533dd) is statically unreachable: every path reaching the sum has either cleared the flag already (entry-flag path) or has a null range pointer (globals path), so its flag test always takes the compare branch; it is recorded as an observation, not as semantics
algorithm.small_path: ranges of at most two elements take the scalar tail path; longer ranges take a SIMD pair loop plus a one- or two-element tail; both paths sum exactly the second qwords of all elements
algorithm.sum: the decision sums only the second qword (offset +0x08) of each 16-byte element, with 64-bit wrapping arithmetic
algorithm.threshold: a sum of at most 0x7fff answers false immediately; otherwise the sum is shifted right by 8 and the answer is (sum >> 8) >= element count

consumers.call_site: single call at 0x5d61e1d in FDE 0x5d60fa0..0x5d623e0; the caller passes its own register rdi (ignored by the routine) and the holder pointer in rsi (a stack slot at rbp-0x250 in the caller, whose first field points at the range)
consumers.false_branch: a zero result falls through to the range-walk append path at 0x5d61e2a
consumers.true_branch: a nonzero result jumps to the 0x60-byte allocation path at 0x5d61f51

global_pair.notes: BSS slots: file-backed bytes of their LOAD segment end before them and memsz covers them, so they start as zero; other code reads them (0x5d62286) and writes a 16-byte pair to them (0x5d83fab), but the producer is not pinned here
global_pair.routine_reads: read at 0x5d53440 (begin) and 0x5d53447 (end) only on the null-pair path

holder_layout.flag: flag byte at holder + 0x10; nonzero means the range is stored reversed
holder_layout.plus_08: the holder's +0x08 qword is never read by the routine; not pinned
holder_layout.range_pointer: holder + 0x00 points at a {begin, end} pair for the 16-byte-element range

main: no calls: the routine is a leaf; all control flow is internal jumps

routines.name: flag-gated range reverse and second-field sum threshold
routines.outputs: al = 1 when the reversed range's scaled second-field sum reaches the element count, else 0

unknowns: What the elements' first qwords mean; the routine never reads them, so the packet does not pin the value side of the range.
What the holder's +0x08 qword holds; the routine never reads it.
Which code owns the holder and the global pair, and what fills them; the packet pins only the routine's reads and the single consumer's branch.
The caller's body beyond the branch at 0x5d61e22; its 0x60-byte allocation path and range-walk append path are named as branch targets only.
Whether the post-sum reversal block was reachable under an older build or a different caller; in this binary it is statically unreachable, as recorded above.
